transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess I came in because I haven’t quite been feeling like myself. It’s not like anything dramatic, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the things I usually care about—like going on photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar organized—have started to feel kind of flat and heavy.

I’ve been having a harder time starting those things, even though I know they’re good for me. I just… don’t initiate them the way I normally would. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way?

I think… probably about a year and three months, give or take. It kind of started after a family member’s health and behavior changed, and I ended up taking on more of the coordinating and managing things. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I noticed I wasn’t bouncing back quite the same.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since you started feeling this way?

I’m not sure I’d say sad or empty most of the time, no. It’s more like… things feel harder to get going, and not as rewarding. I don’t want to sound like I’m being dramatic, because I can still function, but there’s a kind of heaviness sometimes. I don’t know if that counts as empty?
Do you still enjoy the activities you mentioned, like photography walks, when you do manage to start them?

A little, yes… once I actually get myself out there, I can still notice things that are nice, like the light or a good shot. But it’s not the same as it used to be.

The bigger thing is I just don’t start. Photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean—those used to make me feel like me, and lately they feel kind of flat and heavy. I don’t mean I hate them or anything… it’s just harder to feel pulled toward them, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I can still do things if I push myself. But what made me come in is that the things that usually make me feel like myself—photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping a clean calendar—started feeling kind of flat and heavy.

It’s less like I decided I don’t care, and more like I just… stopped initiating them. Does that make sense?
Do you feel pleasure when you are doing things that you used to enjoy?

Some, yeah… I don’t want to say there’s no pleasure at all. If I’m actually out taking pictures, I can still appreciate a good shot or feel a little better for a moment.

But it’s muted, I guess. The things that used to make me feel like myself—photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar neat—they’ve started feeling kind of flat and heavy. And I just don’t start them the way I used to. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Not that I’ve really noticed, no. I mean… my clothes seem to fit about the same, I think. I haven’t been tracking it closely, so I don’t want to give you a wrong answer, but nothing significant has stood out to me.
Have you had periods like this before in your life?

I’ve had little stretches where I get less motivated, sure… I think everyone does. But this feels more noticeable than the usual slump.

What made me come in is that the things that usually make me feel like me—going on photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar cleaned up—started feeling kind of flat and heavy. And I wasn’t really choosing to stop them, exactly… I just stopped starting them. If that makes sense.
Have you had more than one period like this in your life?

More than one? Um… I wouldn’t say it’s been a big pattern, exactly. I’ve had times before where I was less motivated, but this one is the one that really stood out.

Mostly because the things that usually make me feel like myself—like going out for photography, mentoring the kids, keeping my calendar clean—started feeling flat and heavy. And I didn’t really decide to quit them… I just sort of stopped initiating them. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt this way before this current period?

I guess… not quite like this, no. I’ve had off times before, but this current stretch is what made me think, okay, maybe I should talk to someone.

It’s more that the things that usually make me feel like myself—my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar tidy—started feeling kind of flat and heavy. And I wasn’t trying to be lazy or anything… I just stopped starting them. Does that make sense?
Have you had two or more periods like this in your life?

I don’t think I’d call it two or more clear periods, no… at least not in the same way. I’ve had normal dips, I guess, but this is the one that felt different enough to bring me in.

Like I said, what worried me was that photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar clean—things that usually make me feel like me—started feeling flat and heavy. And I just… stopped initiating them. I hope that answers it the way you mean.
Have you experienced episodes of feeling depressed or flat like this before, and then had periods where you felt completely back to normal?

Not really in a clear “episode, then totally back to normal” kind of way. I mean, I’ve had normal low patches like anyone, but this feels like the one that’s been noticeable.

What made me come in is more that the things that usually make me feel like myself—photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping a clean calendar—started feeling flat and heavy. And I just… stopped initiating them. I don’t want to overstate it, but that part didn’t feel like me. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you had any periods in your life where you felt completely back to normal after feeling depressed or flat?

I’m not sure I’d say there were clear times like that, where I was depressed and then completely back to normal. Maybe I’m not tracking it the right way.

The main thing I’ve noticed is what I mentioned before—stuff that usually makes me feel like myself, like going out for photography, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar organized… it started feeling heavy and kind of flat. And I just stopped getting myself to start those things.

I don’t know if that counts as not being “back to normal,” but that’s the part that felt off to me.
Have your feelings of heaviness and lack of interest in activities affected your relationships with family or friends, or your work performance?

A little, yeah… though I wouldn’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart. Work is mostly still intact. I’m getting things done.

But I have noticed I’m missing little calendar details, or I have to double-check tasks that used to be automatic for me. That’s not really like me, so it bothers me.

And socially, I’ve pulled back some. I’m not going out for photography outings much, and I’ve stepped back from mentoring a bit because I don’t feel as present or reliable as I usually am. I hope that makes sense.
Have you ever had a period where you felt completely back to normal after feeling depressed or flat, and then later felt depressed or flat again?

I don’t think I can point to a clean cycle like that—like, “I was flat, then totally myself again, then it came back.” It hasn’t felt that neat to me.

What I keep coming back to is more that the things that normally make me feel like me—photography walks, mentoring, keeping my calendar straight—started feeling kind of heavy and flat, and I stopped being the one to initiate them. I’m not sure if that answers exactly what you’re asking, but that’s the pattern I’ve noticed.
Have you experienced more than two periods in your life where you felt depressed or flat?

I’m not sure I’d count it as more than two separate “periods,” exactly. I don’t want to overstate it.

What made me come in is more that the things that usually make me feel like myself—my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping a clean calendar—started feeling flat and heavy. And I noticed I just wasn’t initiating them like I normally would.

So… yes, I’ve felt that flatness, but I’m not sure I can divide it neatly into distinct episodes, if that’s what you mean.
Have you had more than two periods in your life where you felt similar to how you're feeling now?

I think… I may have sort of answered this already, sorry. I’m not sure I can honestly separate it into “more than two periods” in a clean way.

What I can say is that what made me come in is this same feeling where the things that usually make me feel like myself—going on photography walks, mentoring the kids, even just keeping my calendar clean—started feeling flat and heavy. And I just kind of stopped initiating them.

So, similar to now, yes… but I don’t want to make it sound more definite than it is. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you had two or more episodes of feeling depressed or flat in your life, including this current one?

I’m not sure I can honestly say “two or more episodes” in a clear way. I don’t want to give you a yes if I’m not really sure.

What I can say is that this time, what made me come in was that the things that usually make me feel like myself—photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar clean—started feeling flat and heavy, and I just stopped being the one to start them.

So… I’ve had that kind of flatness, but I’m not sure I can count it neatly as two separate episodes. Is that okay to say?
Have you had any episodes of feeling depressed or flat before this current one that lasted for at least two weeks?

I’m not totally sure about the “at least two weeks” part before this, honestly. I don’t want to say yes just to be agreeable if I can’t place it clearly.

What I do know is what brought me in now: the things that usually make me feel like me—my photography walks, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar tidy—started feeling flat and heavy. And I just wasn’t starting them anymore.

Before now, I may have had stretches like that, but I can’t confidently say they lasted two weeks. Is that okay?
Have you had any episodes of feeling depressed or flat before this current one?

Before this one… I think there were times that felt kind of similar, but I’m a little hesitant to label them as full “episodes,” if that makes sense.

The main thing I recognize is that pattern where the things that usually make me feel like myself—going out for photography, mentoring the kids, even keeping my calendar neat—start to feel flat or heavy, and then I just stop being the one to initiate them.

I don’t want to overstate it, but yes, I’ve noticed that kind of flatness before. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
